research_question: Do inferred duplicate-content links improve binary rumor classification beyond observed reply structure when model, data, features, and training conditions are matched?
outer_evaluation: Leave one entire event out. Each conversation is test data exactly once. No conversation from the held-out event is used for training, validation, vocabulary fitting, checkpoint selection, or matching-rule decisions in that fold.
inner_validation: Within the other events, reserve a stratified random 15% of conversations for checkpoint selection with split seed 20261019. The same train/validation membership is used for both graph conditions and all model seeds in that event fold.

primary_comparison.reply_only: Observed reply tree; no duplicate-content edges or duplicate metadata.
primary_comparison.reply_plus_inferred_duplicates: Same posts and reply tree plus within-conversation exact-text links between existing posts.
primary_comparison.matching_rule: Trim outer whitespace and lowercase; link complete non-empty exact text matches only. Do not add nodes, fuzzy matches, cross-conversation links, or verified-reshares claims.
primary_comparison.edge_direction: Earlier timestamp to later timestamp; input order breaks timestamp ties. If any post in a thread lacks a parseable created_at value, use deterministic structure traversal order for all posts in that thread. This is a computational convention, not verified provenance.

controlled_conditions.architecture: Same ARAGCL-DP GCN encoder and classifier for both graph conditions.
controlled_conditions.augmentation: Uniform random augmentation for both conditions; no centrality-based intervention in this comparison.
controlled_conditions.augmentation_randomness_limit: Both conditions use the same rates and stage seeds, but added duplicate edges consume additional edge-drop draws, so realized views need not be identical. The estimate is the total pipeline effect of including the links, not an edge-only intervention under identical sampled views.
controlled_conditions.features: Character TF-IDF, character n-grams 1-2, maximum 2048 features; fit on inner training posts only within each outer fold.
controlled_conditions.matched_initialization: Same initialized model weights per outer fold and seed across graph conditions.
controlled_conditions.training_order: Fixed conversation order shared by conditions; all condition and seed choices are logged.

checkpoint_selection: Maximum validation Macro-F1; first epoch wins ties. The held-out event is evaluated once after checkpoint restoration.
primary_metric: Macro-F1 over rumor and non-rumor classes, computed from pooled out-of-fold predictions per seed.
paired_analysis: Compare both conditions on identical held-out conversations. Report per-seed out-of-fold results and paired metric differences; do not treat seeds as independent data samples or claim a p-value from seed variation alone.
incomplete_data_policy: Exclude unclear labels and any thread whose structure node lacks a tweet JSON; record every exclusion. Do not synthesize missing text. Retain multiple top-level components as an observed forest, mark each component root, and do not invent reply links between components.
prohibited_after_test: Do not use held-out event outcomes to alter the matching rule, hyperparameters, model architecture, or checkpoint selection. Any follow-up design becomes a new exploratory protocol.
interpretation_limit: The dataset supplies reply structure and binary rumor labels, not verified repost-source IDs. The treatment is inferred exact-content links. Results test whether this specified graph intervention helps on these events; they do not establish universal importance.
